reply:
I found four extra hidden neurons that look deliberately planted, with the code most likely spelled by where each neuron's one large weight sits.

**Four neurons that can't change any move.** Hidden neurons 32–35 send exactly the same weight to all nine move scores: 0.063, −0.042, 0.051 and −0.029. A constant added to every score never changes which cell scores highest. So these four neurons have no effect on play. Every other neuron's weights to the move scores vary in the usual way. Training would not produce four neurons that are perfectly constant like this, so they were almost certainly added by hand.

**Their input weights look hand-written.** The signs mostly alternate, and the values fall into a few repeated sizes (about ±0.1–0.4, ±0.5–0.9, ±1.0–1.4). Each row has exactly one weight near 2.4, well above anything else in that row:

| Neuron | Large weight | Input index | Letter (A=0) | Letter (A=1) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32 | 2.451 | 11 | L | K |
| 33 | 2.382 | 23 | X | W |
| 34 | 2.415 | 13 | N | M |
| 35 | 2.399 | 4 | E | D |

**Other places I checked.** The biases of these neurons (0.231, −0.142, 0.315, −0.054), the digits of the large weights (451, 382, 415, 399) and their constant output weights don't map to letters in any obvious way. The position of the one large weight is the clear signal.

**Which way to read it.** Neither reading spells a word, so the choice of convention is a guess. I went with A=0 (index 0 = A), which gives **LXNE**. That is the usual way to turn letters into positions in code. If the encoder counted from A=1 instead, the code would be **KWMD**.

**Verdict:** I'm confident this network hides something, because of the four neurons that can't affect play. I'm less sure of the exact letters.

PROB: 92
CODE: LXNE
